title: Multi-cluster Path Resilience and Routing Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact playbook for making routing decisions across multiple regions and clusters while prioritizing path resilience, predictable failover, and minimum blast radius for tenant isolation. It’s intended as a pragmatic complement to longer design docs — focused on operator-visible behaviors, configuration knobs, and a small matrix of failure scenarios we must handle.

Assumptions and scope:
- Applies to the platform control-plane and data-plane interactions that influence routing (API gateway, regional proxies, mesh control-plane components).
- Covers HTTP/gRPC request paths for inference traffic, metadata/callbacks, and observability telemetry.
- Does NOT specify model-specific fallback logic (that belongs in serving/runtime docs), but includes hooks for routing to compatible model variants.
- Targets multi-region topologies (2+ regions) and multi-cluster within region.

Design goals (ranked):
1) Keep end-user tail latency within SLOs by preferring local-region routes when healthy.
2) Achieve deterministic degraded behavior — explicit fallback paths rather than probabilistic blackhole.
3) Minimize cross-region egress cost by tiering fallback choices.
4) Retain per-tenant isolation properties: no automatic cross-tenant routing into another customer’s dedicated capacity.

Routing policy primitives we expose:
- preference: local | regional-peer | global
- affinity: none | session | client-ip | token (sticky by API key)
- cost_weight: numeric factor used by optimizer to bias lower-cost routes
- latency_margin_ms: allowed additional latency above local median before failover triggers
- allow_cross_region_egress: boolean (explicit per-route policy)
- fallback_order: ordered list of model/service endpoints by compatibility

Control plane behavior (runtime expectations):
- Fast-path config: edge proxies cache routing decisions for 10s with TTL jitter; control plane publishes updates via push + delta.
- Reconciliation: control plane writes authoritative route maps to a distributed store; regional controllers subscribe and validate consistency every 30s.
- Leaderless decisioning: prefer locally-run regional controllers to avoid single global control-plane dependency for route decisions. Global control plane only supplies policy defaults and rollout plan.
- Safe deploys: any change that widens allow_cross_region_egress requires a 2-step approval + canary traffic in a sandbox region.

mTLS and identity model notes:
- mTLS termination options:
  - Sidecar-terminated (recommended for internal pod-to-pod): mutual TLS with short-lived certs issued by regional CA, rotated every 12h.
  - Gateway-terminated (for external ingress/egress): TLS terminated at gateway, then mTLS onward to backend depending on trust boundary.
- Trust model: regional CAs chained to a global root that only the control plane holds. Cross-region trust requires explicit CA distribution and pinned roots in each region.
- Certificate lifecycle: automatic enrollment via SVID-style workflow (controller issues CSR -> CA returns cert). If cert rotation fails, traffic should degrade to gateway-terminated TLS only — but only if route policy allows non-mTLS (explicit opt-in).

Service mesh considerations and tradeoffs:
- Centralized mesh control plane (single global) gives uniform policy but increases blast radius and cross-region latency for policy reads. Not recommended for control of failover decisions.
- Federated mesh control plane (regional controllers + global policy sync) is preferred: quick local decisions, consistent policy surface. Use reconciliation windows to detect drift.
- Sidecars vs gateway-only:
  - Sidecars provide per-pod identity and fine-grained mTLS, easier to enforce mutual auth and telemetry. But increases CPU overhead and adds scaling concerns in very high-throughput inference pods.
  - Gateway-only reduces per-pod overhead but loses strong mutual authentication between pods. Consider gateway-only for inference workers behind a strict network ACL and require additional eBPF-level enforcement.

Failure scenarios and operator runbook (condensed):
1) Regional control-plane outage (control-plane leader fails):
   - Regional proxies switch to cached routing for up to TTL (default 10s).
   - If outage > TTL, regional controller falls back to global defaults (read-only mode) and record audit.
   - If leaders not elected within 90s, fail open to regional-peers with cost_weight penalty.
2) Inter-region WAN partition:
   - If allow_cross_region_egress=false, traffic stays local — degrade with 503s for requests that require remote-only model variants and alert.
   - If allow_cross_region_egress=true, route to next-best regional replica with additional latency_margin_ms applied; track egress metrics separately for billing.
3) Mesh data-plane certificate expiry:
   - Automatically rotate via controller. If rotation fails, set READ-ONLY mode for deployments that require mutual auth; route traffic through gateway-termination if policy permits.
4) Downstream service capacity exhaustion in region:
   - Immediate apply traffic shaping and queueing at ingress, then incrementally shift to regional-peers up to configured spill percentage (default 20% every 30s) to avoid sudden bursts.

Operational knobs and SLOs (suggested):
- routing-decision-cache-ttl: 10s default (operator adjustable 5–60s)
- controller-reconcile-interval: 30s
- max-cross-region-egress-percent: per-tenant default 10% (escalate via billing/report)
- failover-time-target: 3 x median p50 latency for local route or 250ms whichever is smaller
- telemetry: tag every request with origin-region, chosen-route, route-reason, and egress-cost-tag for billing

Testing and validation checklist before rollout:
- Simulate regional control-plane lag (saturate CR QPS) and assert fallbacks within TTL.
- WAN partition tests between regions with injected latency and packet loss; validate cost tagging and billing pipeline.
- Certificate rotation chaos test: rotate CA and certs in a canary cluster and monitor auth failures and recovery time.
- Cost sensitivity: run synthetic workload to measure cross-region egress cost growth under spillover scenarios.

Open questions / action items:
- Define default per-tenant max-cross-region-egress percent and how it ties to billing alerts (owner: Product - Sana).
- Decide exact cert lifetime and rotation window for inference-sidecars vs control-plane (owner: Security - Jonas).
- Add control-plane read-only mode telemetry so SRE can distinguish cached behavior vs authoritative routing (owner: Platform - Marina).

References and links:
- Confluence draft: Multi-Cluster Routing Patterns (linked above).
- GitHub PR for regional controller: /platform/pull/1589 (contains proto changes for route metadata).
- JIRA playground: PLAT-4021 for rollout plan and canary schedule.

Appendix: simple routing decision matrix (text):
- If (local healthy && latency <= median + latency_margin) -> choose local
- Else if (local overloaded && allow_spill && regional-peer available && cost_weight acceptable) -> spill to regional-peer
- Else if (cross-region allowed && global replica available) -> route to global replica (mark egress cost)
- Else -> fail with explicit 503 + structured error suggesting retry window and recommended fallback

Notes: keep this doc lightweight and iterate. This is an operational playbook, not the final API surface. Add more examples from real incidents after first 2 region rollouts.
